chunks: Or have you become so unafraid that He who is in Heaven will not send a violent wind to shower stones at you? Then you will know the import of My commination!

key_terms.مَن فِي السَّمَاءِ: He who is in the heaven (referring to God)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'He who is in the heaven' sending a 'hassin' (wind with stones)?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from the arrogance of worldly power to the humility of recognizing divine authority, often linked to the concept of *Tawhid* in action. The 'stones' (*hasib*) are interpreted not merely as physical hail but as a metaphor for sudden, inescapable retribution that exposes the fragility of human claims to sovereignty. This serves as a profound reminder for believers to maintain spiritual vigilance against the illusion of self-sufficiency.
